thread:
support_lead: @eng-sre FYI ACME Ads on hosted-usw2 reporting p95 jump from ~140ms -> ~1.2s starting ~03:12 UTC. Customer request id: req-5f4d2a. They see many client retries.

acct_mgr_alex: Customer says this started after your maintenance window (03:00). They're losing ad impressions. Escalating.

eng_sre_ben: checking dashboards now. Is there a rollout/driver change at 03:00?

infra_dave: we pushed driver 537.21 + CUDA 13.1 modules to us-west clusters at 02:58-03:05 for two node pools (uw2-pool-x, uw2-pool-y). Also a firmware staging push to rack r21 at 02:50. No automatic rollback.

runtime_carmen: can you paste host-level logs? want to see NVMe/hostfs behavior and KV cache hits.

infra_dave: logs from uw2-pool-x-node04 around event time:
```
Mar 18 03:10:12 uw2-pool-x-node04 kernel: nvme nvme1: I/O 310 ms, qid 1
Mar 18 03:11:07 uw2-pool-x-node04 kernel: nvme nvme1: controller reset due to I/O timeout
Mar 18 03:11:33 uw2-pool-x-node04 kernel: nvme nvme1n1: aborting command 0x3a status:0x2
```

infra_dave: hostfs latencies spiked too: pre-update p95/p99 9ms/60ms -> post-update 45ms/1.1s on those hosts.

eng_sre_ben: that matches the p95/p99 seen by the customer. runtime_carmen: can model runtime be waiting on disk?

runtime_carmen: yes traces show stalls at startup for kv cache loads. GPU compute threads idle waiting for pagein ~50-600ms per file; cumulative adds up for small requests. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 98% -> 78% for affected traffic.

support_lead: customer repro (from them):
```
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-chat-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short prompt"}],"max_tokens":64}' &
done
# observed p95 ~1.1s
```

acct_mgr_alex: they're asking for an immediate mitigation and ETA for a safe fix.

eng_sre_ben: short-term mitigations: 1) failover ACME traffic to a non-rolled pool (uw2-dedicated-2) 2) pin their model to rw-chat-2-small (smaller KV footprint) 3) temporarily disable KV prefetch on warm starts for that customer

infra_dave: starting traffic migration to uw2-dedicated-2 now. Also increasing nvme_core.io_timeout to 120s on rolled hosts to avoid resets while we triage.

deploy_bot: Routing change applied: 100% of traffic for acct:acme -> uw2-dedicated-2 at 03:28 UTC (req-id: route-77b).

eng_sre_ben: after migration p95 dropped to ~180ms for ACME (03:32). Rolling rollback of driver on uw2-pool-x and uw2-pool-y starting (reverting to 536.90).

infra_dave: rollback in progress. Also isolating rack r21 firmware target to avoid further hardware noise.

runtime_carmen: after rollback + KV prefetch off, KV cache hit ratio returned to ~96% and GPU stalls largely disappeared in traces.

eng_sre_ben: kernel nvme errors stopped on rolled hosts once driver reverted.

support_lead: told customer we'll keep them on dedicated pool until we validate a safe rollout. They confirmed service restored and will monitor.

incident-bot: ACTION CREATED - INCIDENT-2026-1457 assigned to eng-infra severity: P2

eng_sre_ben: post-incident action items (owners):
- Add a canary nvme firmware/driver integration test that runs hostfs stress on real NVMe (owner: infra_dave)
- Runtime change: add hostfs burst queuing and backoff for KV cache prefetch to limit concurrent page-in storms (owner: runtime_carmen)
- Add an automated alert that correlates p95/p99 spikes with nvme controller errors and triggers traffic reroute (owner: eng_sre_ben)
- Revisit rollout runbook to include immediate traffic-drain cutover option (owner: infra_dave)

acct_mgr_alex: customer requested timeline for safe re-rollout. We will provide ETA after infra validation tests.

eng_sre_ben: closing active customer-facing escalation; keeping incident open for infra follow-up. :thumbsup:
